arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Donald Verrilli argued the ADEA protects workers over forty from disparate treatment.
He stated the law rejects the assumption that competence declines with age.
Paul Clement argued the ADEA prohibits discrimination against the protected class.
He contended the law is not limited to claims by the oldest members of the class.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: General Dynamics Land Systems argues the law protects only the oldest workers in a group. Dennis Cline argues the law protects all workers over forty from age bias.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: General Dynamics wants the Court to limit ADEA protection to the oldest workers in a group.
Cline wants the Court to confirm ADEA protection covers all workers over forty.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: General Dynamics argues the statute requires comparing workers to the oldest members of the group.
Cline argues the statute prohibits bias against any worker over forty based on age.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the scope of federal age-discrimination protections for workers over forty. It determines whether employers can dismiss older workers if younger colleagues remain in the group. This rule shapes workplace hiring and retention practices nationwide.
